messages.subject: SECR trend analysis query
messages.body_plain:
I have an query regarding SECR
say I have sampled 100 sqkm area in 1st year, 150 sqkm in 2nd area , 200 sqkm in 3rd year( the increased area included the 1st year sampling area). if we buffer the area for mask (area of integration), my masked area will be same for all the three years because of  removal of non habitat area beyond the suggested buffer of sampling area(mcp).  So for seeing density trend should I choose the 100sqkm area of all the three years or SECR models allows to use data available from different sampling area if mask area is same for all the years.
Do we have option to run in SECR for trend analysis.?

messages.subject: Re: SECR trend analysis query
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ujjwal

I don't think there is any problem for SECR models that parameterise abundance as density: density comparisons are valid even when the area changes. There is no specific reason to use the same mask, but I guess that reduces the possibility that changing area itself caused a change in average density if density is patchy.

I assume the different years are different secr 'sessions' in your analysis. Then for equally spaced sessions D ~ Session is a linear trend model on the log scale (equivalent to Pradel's lambda). Note the capital S! The trend is given by the fitted 'beta' coefficient. If you want to fit a linear trend on the natural scale then set link=list(D='identity') in secr.fit().

Hope this makes it clear.
Murray

messages.subject: Re: unit of a0 in Efford and Mowat 2014.??
messages.subject_clean: unit of a0 in Efford and Mowat 2014.??
messages.body_plain:
I replied to mayank offline, and forgot this was left unanswered. It's probably easiest to understand by starting with the effective sampling area 'a'. That has units of area (km^2) and gives an estimate of density from D-hat = n / a-hat where n is the number of detected individuals. In that way it is 'like' detection probability (p where N-hat = n / p-hat). It can be helpful (for reasons explained in Efford and Mowat) to fit models parameterised by D, a and sigma, but these are somewhat awkward to fit. As a 'cheap' alternative we can define a quantity a0 that varies like 'a' and also has units of area but differs (roughly) by some unknown constant.
Murray

messages.subject: RE: simulate sex-specific detection parameters
messages.body_plain:
HI Eric,

I think the sim.pop function is just simulating the locations of individuals. Rather, you might want to try one of the other simulation functions (e.g. ?sim.secr() or ?sim.capthist()) which will also (I think) generate capture histories according to a defined encounter model.

There are probably a few other ways that someone else can recommend as always is the case with these types of things.

Chris

messages.body_plain:
[I seem to have sent only a personal reply before - now posting also to list]

This is a significant bug in the software, introduced in the recent version. An internal check on the model argument fails with CL = TRUE when no model is specified (i.e. the default is used). It seems you can get around it by providing a null model argument:

fit0CL<- secr.fit(CH,mask=mask,CL=T, model = g0~1)

Thanks for reporting this. I'll fix it ASAP.
Murray

messages.body_plain:

Hi Ujjwal
For CL = T density does not appear in the model, but you have D ~ session. That is a real error, not the spurious one Mayank turned up earlier. In fact you automatically get session-specific estimates of D from derived() even with CL = T because it uses the session-specific n in the formula D = n/a.
Murray

messages.subject: trouble with trap.builder
messages.body_plain:
Good day,
We are attempting to simulate camera-trap sampling within a national park.  We'd like to simulate different trap layouts.
I created a cluster of traps as a traps object using make.grid and subset:
#
tenX500 = make.grid(nx = 21, ny = 21, spacex = 500, spacey = 500, detector = "proximity")
#
cross12 = subset(tenX500, subset = c("A11","I11","J11","K 1","K 9",'K10',"K12","K13","K21","L11","M11","U11"))
#
This gives a 10 km X 10 km box or cross shape defined by 4 traps, with a smaller 2 km X 2 km "X" or cross shape in the center.
We have the park boundary as a SpatialPolygonsDataFrame (knpb.spdf).  I used it (with gBuffer and make.mask) to define a finite sampling frame for trap.builder:
#
knp.interior = gBuffer(knpb.spdf, width = -4000)
df = data.frame(1)
knp.int <http://knp.int> = SpatialPolygonsDataFrame(knp.interior, df, match.ID = F)
#
fr.mask = make.mask(spacing = 1000, type = c("polygon"), poly = knp.int <http://knp.int>)
#
fr = as.data.frame(fr.mask)
#
This gives me a finite sampling frame with points 1000 m apart, all of which are at least 4000 m inside the park boundary.
However, when I try to use trap.builder with edgemethod = c("allinside"), I get error messages
#
> l1 = trap.builder(n = 4, cluster = cross12, region = knpb.spdf, frame = fr,
+ method = c("GRTS"),edgemethod = c("allinside"),detector = "proximity",
+ samplefactor = 10, plt = TRUE)
Stratum: None
Current number of levels: 3
Current number of levels: 5
Final number of levels: 5
Error in trap.builder(n = 4, cluster = cross12, region = knpb.spdf, frame = fr,  :
  not enough clusters inside polygon
> l1 = trap.builder(n = 4, cluster = cross12, region = knpb.spdf, frame = fr,
+ method = c("GRTS"),edgemethod = c("allinside"),detector = "proximity",
+ samplefactor = 100, plt = TRUE)
Stratum: None
Current number of levels: 5
Current number of levels: 7
Current number of levels: 8
Current number of levels: 9
Final number of levels: 9
Error in origins[i, ] : subscript out of bounds
In addition: There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)
#
I tried setting edgemethod = "clip" to see if that was the only problem, and got a different error message.
#
> l1 = trap.builder(n = 4, cluster = cross12, region = knpb.spdf, frame = fr,
+ method = c("GRTS"),edgemethod = c("clip"),detector = "proximity",
+ samplefactor = 10, plt = TRUE)
Stratum: None
Current number of levels: 3
Current number of levels: 5
Final number of levels: 5
Error in `row.names<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, value = c("1.A11", "1.I11",  :
  duplicate 'row.names' are not allowed
In addition: Warning message:
non-unique value when setting 'row.names': ‘NA.NA <http://NA.NA>’

Not sure what I'm doing wrong here, but any advice would be welcome.
Thanks,
Eric

messages.subject: Re: trouble with trap.builder
messages.body_plain:
Eric

I think we are getting different results because the attributes of your SPDF (knpb.spdf) include NA values and mine don't. This shouldn't be a problem, except that the test for 'allinside' in trap.builder (mistakenly) expects the 'over' method of 'sp' to return only a vector of nonmissing values, whereas the return value includes attributes if they are present in the input. The attributes are not really relevant, and I'll re-engineer trap.builder to avoid them. Meantime, it seems that you can work around simply by calling trap.builder with region = polygons(knpb.spdf) instead of region = knpb.spdf.

Let me know if that doesn't work!

Murray

messages.subject: Re: simulate sex-specific detection parameters
messages.body_plain:
After looking at the documentation for rbind.capthist (and MS.capthist), I was able to generate simulated data under sex-specific densities and detection parameters two ways: sex as 2 sessions, and sex as an individual covariate.  Example code below.

############## Sex as session
#
test.pop.F = sim.popn(D = 0.010, core = syst.trap, buffer = 500, model2D = ("poisson"), buffertype = "rect")
test.pop.M = sim.popn(D = 0.005, core = syst.trap, buffer = 500, model2D = ("poisson"), buffertype = "rect")
#
test.chF = sim.capthist(syst.trap, test.pop.F, detectfn = 0, detectpar = list(g0 = 0.1, sigma = 300), noccasions = 8)
test.chM = sim.capthist(syst.trap, test.pop.M, detectfn = 0, detectpar = list(g0 = 0.15, sigma = 1500), noccasions = 8)
#
test.ch <http://test.ch> = MS.capthist(F = test.chF, M = test.chM)
#
test.fit = secr.fit (test.ch <http://test.ch>, model = list(g0~session, sigma~session), mask = rect.mask, CL = TRUE) # works
#
### end script
#
#
############### Sex as individual covariate
#
#
tpop.sexF = sim.popn(D = 0.010, core = syst.trap, buffer = 500, model2D = ("poisson"), buffertype = "rect",
 covariates = list(sex = c(F = 1.0, M = 0.0)))
tpop.sexM = sim.popn(D = 0.005, core = syst.trap, buffer = 500, model2D = ("poisson"), buffertype = "rect",
 covariates = list(sex = c(F = 0.0, M = 1.0)))
#
#
tch.F = sim.capthist(syst.trap, tpop.sexF, detectfn = 0, detectpar = list(g0 = 0.1, sigma = 300), noccasions = 8)
#
tch.M = sim.capthist(syst.trap, tpop.sexM, detectfn = 0, detectpar = list(g0 = 0.15, sigma = 1500), noccasions = 8)
#
tch = rbind.capthist(tch.F, tch.M)
#
tfit = secr.fit (tch, model = list(g0~sex, sigma~sex), mask = rect.mask, CL = TRUE)
#
### end script

Cheers,
Eric

messages.subject_clean: error message from validate() in secrdesign; "missing values not allowed..."
messages.body_plain:
Hi Eric
It looks like I didn't cover the NaN case... Damn. You can see the code for validate() (type name at R prompt). I haven't time to check it just now, but I expect sourcing or cutting and pasting this version will fix the problem. is.na <http://is.na>() covers both NA and NaN. If this doesn't work... maybe troubleshoot further?
Murray

validate <- function (x, test, validrange = c(0, Inf), targets = test)
{
    onescenario <- function(scen, minx, maxx) {
        criterion <- (scen[, test] < minx) | (scen[, test] >
            maxx)
        ####################################
        criterion[is.na(criterion)] <- TRUE     ## 2014-10-30
        ####################################
        scen[criterion, targets] <- NA
        scen[is.na(scen[, test]), targets] <- NA
        scen
    }
    if (!inherits(x, "selectedstatistics"))
        stop("requires 'selectedstatistics'")
    if (tolower(targets) == "all")
        targets <- colnames(x$output[[1]])
    if (!all(c(test, targets) %in% colnames(x$output[[1]])))
        stop("test or targets not found in input")
    nscen <- length(x$output)
    if (!is.matrix(validrange))
        validrange <- matrix(validrange, byrow = TRUE, nrow = nscen,
            ncol = 2)
    if (nrow(validrange) != nscen)
        stop("invalid `validrange'")
    minx <- validrange[, 1]
    maxx <- validrange[, 2]
    x$output <- mapply(onescenario, x$output, minx, maxx, SIMPLIFY = FALSE)
    x
}
